description: Circular regulatory sign with a blue face, red border and a single red diagonal slash, prohibiting parking.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim galvanised post carrying a flat circular plate near the top, plate face solid blue with a wide red annular border band around its circumference and one bold red diagonal bar running corner to corner across the blue centre, a smaller rectangular white supplementary plate mounted on the post directly below carrying black lettering reading the Thai line ห้ามจอด above a smaller roman line reading NO PARKING Materials: Blue retroreflective sheeting dulled and chalky, red border and diagonal bar faded toward orange, galvanised post with rust at the ground line, road spatter and adhesive sticker residue on the lower plate.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m, measured by the harness. 544 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. The structural decision of this prop is the MERGE: the supplementary NO PARKING plate is folded into the disc's buffer rather than given its own component, which is the whole reason the prop fits two draw calls. The third material and third geometry were both available and neither was spent - a separate material for the white plate would have been the easy route to a blue disc and a white plate and would have cost a draw call as well.

featureReviews.evidence: 72 radial segments, 288 of the prop's 544 triangles, and the only place triangles are deliberately spent. The rim reads as a true circle at every turntable azimuth and edge-on the disc reads as a thin plate rather than a wedge.

Disc and supplementary plate merged into ONE BufferGeometry: same material, same plane, never moving relative to each other. They share the plane z=+0.0145 to +0.0265 but do not overlap - a 0.32 m vertical gap separates the disc's bottom edge at y=1.70 from the plate's top at y=1.61 - and coplanar co-facing surfaces that do not overlap cannot z-fight. Plate width 0.46 m from the reference's own ratio of 285 px to the disc's 372 px applied to the declared 0.6 m disc, which confirms the plate is narrower than the disc and so does not set the prop's width.

Red border 1.00R to 0.83R read off the x=520 scanline, blue field #337AB9, diagonal slash and both supplementary legend lines, all riding ONE atlas on ONE material along with the bare aluminium back. The slash runs upper-left to lower-right and that is CHIRAL - a slash the other way is a different sign - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored. The slash's separate measurement of #BF7358 against the border's #BF6149 was correctly read as the key's work rather than a second red.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 14 height segments, no texture, with a distinct clean stub above the disc from a separate 446-px crop. Rust #725642 held below 0.28 m with a hard splash line because the per-band scan reads 0 per cent from y=520 to y=860 then 42 and 58 per cent below. Scored lowest of the four on purpose: the clean value rests on only 186 neutral pixels of a 3240 px crop, because this is the most weathered post of the eight, and a top stop resting on 186 pixels is the thinnest measurement anywhere in this spec. The scan's 46 per cent reading at y=480 was discarded as the disc's RED BORDER passing the orange filter rather than rust.
